From Wiktionary, the free dictionary From Yiddish, probably from יאָנץ (yonts). IPA(key): /jʌts/ Rhymes: -ʌts yutz (plural yutzes) (US, derogatory) A foolish, incompetent, awkward, or contemptible person. yutz (third-person singular simple present yutzes, present participle yutzing, simple past and past participle yutzed) (slang, intransitive) To waste time. synonyms ▲Synonyms: futz, putter, putz I'm not busy, I'm just yutzing around on Wiktionary.
